title: [DEBT] ADO.Oracle and ADO.Sqlite SQL scripts use incorrect SQL Server syntax
body:
## Type

- [x] Incorrect implementation

## Description

The SQL scripts in `Encina.ADO.Oracle` and `Encina.ADO.Sqlite` packages use SQL Server-specific syntax that will NOT work on their target databases.

## Location

- **File(s)**: 
  - `src/Encina.ADO.Oracle/Scripts/000_CreateAllTables.sql`
  - `src/Encina.ADO.Sqlite/Scripts/000_CreateAllTables.sql`
- **Package(s)**: Encina.ADO.Oracle, Encina.ADO.Sqlite

## Current Behavior

Scripts contain SQL Server syntax:
- `sys.objects`, `OBJECT_ID()` - SQL Server system views
- `GO` - SQL Server batch separator
- `PRINT` - SQL Server command
- `NVARCHAR(MAX)` - Not valid in SQLite
- `DATETIME2(7)` - Not valid in SQLite/Oracle
- `BIT` - Not valid in Oracle
- `dbo` schema prefix - SQL Server specific

## Expected Behavior

- **Oracle**: Scripts should use PL/SQL syntax with proper Oracle data types (VARCHAR2, CLOB, NUMBER, TIMESTAMP, etc.)
- **SQLite**: Scripts should use SQLite syntax with proper data types (TEXT, INTEGER, REAL, BLOB)

## Root Cause

Scripts were likely copy-pasted from SqlServer implementation without proper adaptation.

## Proposed Fix

### For Oracle (`src/Encina.ADO.Oracle/Scripts/`):
```sql
-- Use PL/SQL syntax
BEGIN
    EXECUTE IMMEDIATE 'CREATE TABLE OutboxMessages (...)';
EXCEPTION
    WHEN OTHERS THEN
        IF SQLCODE != -955 THEN RAISE; END IF;
END;
/
```

### For SQLite (`src/Encina.ADO.Sqlite/Scripts/`):
```sql
-- Use IF NOT EXISTS
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS OutboxMessages (
    Id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    NotificationType TEXT NOT NULL,
    Content TEXT NOT NULL,
    CreatedAtUtc TEXT NOT NULL,
    ...
);
```

- [x] **High** - Blocks functionality or causes failures in production
- [ ] **Medium** - Should be fixed before 1.0 release
- [ ] **Low** - Nice to have, can be deferred

## Effort Estimate

title: [DEBT] Implement LoggerMessage source generators (CA1848)
body:
## Type

- [x] Performance optimization

## Description

Multiple packages suppress CA1848 warning using `#pragma warning disable CA1848`. This warning indicates that we should use LoggerMessage source generators for high-performance logging instead of the extension method overloads.

## Location

- **File(s)**: Most files in messaging transport packages
- **Package(s)**: 
  - Encina.Wolverine
  - Encina.NServiceBus
  - Encina.RabbitMQ
  - Encina.AzureServiceBus
  - Encina.AmazonSQS
  - Encina.Kafka
  - Encina.Redis.PubSub
  - Encina.InMemory
  - Encina.NATS
  - Encina.MQTT
  - Encina.gRPC
  - Encina.GraphQL

## Current Behavior

```csharp
#pragma warning disable CA1848 // Use LoggerMessage delegates
_logger.LogInformation("Processing message {MessageId}", messageId);
#pragma warning restore CA1848
```

## Expected Behavior

```csharp
// In Log.cs (partial class)
internal static partial class Log
{
    [LoggerMessage(EventId = 1, Level = LogLevel.Information, Message = "Processing message {MessageId}")]
    public static partial void ProcessingMessage(ILogger logger, string messageId);
}

// Usage
Log.ProcessingMessage(_logger, messageId);
```

## Root Cause

Initial implementation prioritized functionality over performance optimization.

## Proposed Fix

1. Create `Log.cs` partial class in each package (like `Encina.Dapper.SqlServer/Log.cs`)
2. Define LoggerMessage methods with appropriate EventIds
3. Replace logger extension method calls with static partial method calls
4. Remove `#pragma warning disable CA1848` suppressions

title: [REFACTOR] Apply Orchestrator pattern to Encina.Caching (8 packages)
body:
## Summary

Apply the successful Orchestrator/Store/Factory pattern (used in Encina.Messaging) to the Caching subsystem to centralize domain logic and reduce code duplication across 8 caching providers.

## Motivation

- [ ] Code duplication
- [ ] Poor separation of concerns
- [x] Applying a design pattern (specify: Orchestrator/Store/Factory pattern)
- [ ] Simplifying complex code
- [ ] Improving testability
- [ ] Performance optimization
- [ ] Preparing for future feature work
- [ ] Other: ___

## Current Structure

Each caching provider (Memory, Hybrid, Redis, Garnet, Valkey, Dragonfly, KeyDB) has its own:
- `CachingPipelineBehavior` implementation (duplicated logic)
- Direct coupling between behavior and provider-specific code

### Files with duplicated logic:
- `src/Encina.Caching.Memory/CachingPipelineBehavior.cs`
- `src/Encina.Caching.Hybrid/CachingPipelineBehavior.cs`
- `src/Encina.Caching.Redis/CachingPipelineBehavior.cs`
- `src/Encina.Caching.Garnet/CachingPipelineBehavior.cs`
- `src/Encina.Caching.Valkey/CachingPipelineBehavior.cs`
- `src/Encina.Caching.Dragonfly/CachingPipelineBehavior.cs`
- `src/Encina.Caching.KeyDB/CachingPipelineBehavior.cs`

## Proposed Structure

```
Encina.Caching (abstractions)
├── ICacheProvider (interface) ← EXISTING
├── ICacheKeyGenerator (interface) ← EXISTING  
├── CacheOrchestrator (domain logic) ← NEW: centralized caching orchestration
└── CachingPipelineBehavior (generic) ← CENTRALIZE: uses CacheOrchestrator

Encina.Caching.* (providers)
├── *CacheProvider (implements ICacheProvider) ← EXISTING
└── ServiceCollectionExtensions (registers CacheOrchestrator) ← UPDATE
```

### Expected Improvement

| Metric | Before | After | Improvement |
|--------|--------|-------|-------------|
| Duplicated lines | ~300-400 | ~50-80 | ~40% reduction |
| Files with behavior logic | 7+ | 1 | Single source of truth |
| Maintenance burden | High | Low | Changes in one place |

## Affected Files

- `src/Encina.Caching/CacheOrchestrator.cs` (NEW)
- `src/Encina.Caching/CachingPipelineBehavior.cs` (CENTRALIZE)
- `src/Encina.Caching.Memory/CachingPipelineBehavior.cs` (REMOVE)

- [x] Encina.Caching.Dragonfly

## Behavioral Guarantee

- [x] Existing unit tests cover the refactored code
- [ ] Existing integration tests validate behavior
- [ ] New tests added to cover refactoring safety

title: [BUG] Marten audit projections unregisterable: IServiceProvider parameter rejected by JasperFx validation
body:
## Description

`AuditEntryProjection.Create` and `ReadAuditEntryProjection.Create` in `Encina.Audit.Marten` accept `IServiceProvider` as their second parameter. Marten/JasperFx projection validation rejects this type at store initialization, so `ConfigureMartenAuditProjections.Configure(StoreOptions)` **throws before the store can be used**.

As a result, any application calling `services.AddEncinaAuditMarten(...)` will fail at boot. This bug has gone undetected because `Encina.Audit.Marten` has **no integration tests** (no `tests/Encina.IntegrationTests/AuditMarten/` folder exists) — only unit tests that call `projection.Create(evt, services)` directly, bypassing Marten's projection graph validation.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install `Encina.Audit.Marten` in any app with a real PostgreSQL connection.
2. Register the audit store:
   ```csharp
   services.AddEncinaAuditMarten(options =>
   {
       options.TemporalGranularity = TemporalKeyGranularity.Monthly;
   });
   ```
3. Boot the host — Marten runs `ConfigureMartenAuditProjections.Configure(StoreOptions)`.
4. `JasperFx.Events.Projections.InvalidProjectionException` is thrown.

## Expected Behavior

Marten store initialization completes successfully and both audit projections are registered as async projections on the async daemon.

## Actual Behavior

```
JasperFx.Events.Projections.InvalidProjectionException :
Projection Encina.Audit.Marten.Projections.AuditEntryProjection has validation errors:
Create(AuditEntryRecordedEvent, IServiceProvider) : Task<AuditEntryReadModel>
 - Parameter of type 'System.IServiceProvider' is not supported.
   Valid options are:
     - System.Threading.CancellationToken
     - Marten.IDocumentOperations
     - Encina.Audit.Marten.Events.AuditEntryRecordedEvent
     - JasperFx.Events.IEvent
     - JasperFx.Events.IEvent<AuditEntryRecordedEvent>
```

## Environment

- **Encina Version**: 0.13.x (`main`, current `HEAD`)
- **.NET Version**: .NET 10.0
- **OS**: Any (logic bug, not platform-specific)
- **Package(s) Affected**:
  - `Encina.Audit.Marten` (`AuditEntryProjection`, `ReadAuditEntryProjection`, `ConfigureMartenAuditProjections`)

## Code Sample

```csharp
// Minimal reproduction without Marten store boot
using Encina.Audit.Marten.Projections;
using Marten;

var sut = new ConfigureMartenAuditProjections();
var storeOptions = new StoreOptions();
storeOptions.Connection("Host=localhost;Port=5432;Database=test;Username=postgres;Password=postgres");

// Throws InvalidProjectionException on Projections.Add(...)
sut.Configure(storeOptions);
```

Source (`src/Encina.Audit.Marten/Projections/AuditEntryProjection.cs:60-62`):

```csharp
public async Task<AuditEntryReadModel> Create(
    AuditEntryRecordedEvent @event,
    IServiceProvider services)   // ← Marten rejects this parameter
{
    var keyProvider = services.GetRequiredService<ITemporalKeyProvider>();
    // ...
}
```

Same shape in `src/Encina.Audit.Marten/Projections/ReadAuditEntryProjection.cs`.

## Stack Trace

```
   at JasperFx.Events.Projections.EventProjectionApplication`1.AssertMethodValidity()
   at JasperFx.Events.Projections.JasperFxEventProjectionBase`2.AssembleAndAssertValidity()
   at JasperFx.Events.Projections.ProjectionGraph`3.Register(...)
   at JasperFx.Events.Projections.ProjectionGraph`3.Add(...)
   at Encina.Audit.Marten.Projections.ConfigureMartenAuditProjections.Configure(StoreOptions options)
     in src/Encina.Audit.Marten/Projections/ConfigureMartenAuditProjections.cs:line 40
```

## Root Cause

The Marten projection pipeline injects per-event services through `IDocumentOperations`, not `IServiceProvider`. Temporal key providers and options must be resolved via a projection-scoped pattern (custom factory + constructor injection), not by taking the raw DI container as a method parameter.

## Proposed Fix

Refactor both projections to one of the supported Marten patterns:

1. **Preferred — Custom projection factory via `IProjectionSource`**: resolve `ITemporalKeyProvider`, `IOptions<MartenAuditOptions>`, and the logger via constructor injection, and register the projection with a factory that pulls them from DI at store boot.
2. **Alternative — `IDocumentOperations` + session-scoped service lookup**: query temporal keys through `Marten`-managed sessions rather than a raw `IServiceProvider`.
3. Add an **integration test** under `tests/Encina.IntegrationTests/AuditMarten/` that boots a real Marten store (Testcontainers PostgreSQL) and exercises `AddEncinaAuditMarten()` end-to-end. This test would have caught the bug on introduction.

Out of scope for this issue but recommended follow-up: audit all Encina.Marten / Encina.Marten.GDPR projections for the same anti-pattern.

## Related

- Introduced by #800 (`[FEATURE] Add Encina.Audit.Marten`)
- Adjacent Marten bug: #801 (`AggregateStreamAsync does not set Version`) — both discovered by the integration gap
- Tests that worked around this issue (calling `Create` directly with a substitute `IServiceProvider`) added in PR #948

## Additional Context

- Discovered while adding unit/guard coverage for `Encina.Audit.Marten` in PR #948. The `Configure_ValidOptions_RegistersProjectionsAndIndexes` test had to be removed; only the null-guard path remains testable at unit level.
- No `Encina.IntegrationTests/AuditMarten/` folder exists, so the Marten store has never been booted with these projections in CI. Any production app consuming the package would fail immediately.

title: [INFRA] Mutation Tests: widen scope beyond smoke test and fix coverage capture
body:
## Category

- [x] CI/CD Workflow (GitHub Actions)
- [x] Test Infrastructure (fixtures, runners, parallelization)

## Description

Issue #957 resolved the fundamental blockers that prevented the Mutation Tests workflow from completing. The workflow is now green with a smoke-test scope (`**/Sharding/Migrations/Strategies/*.cs`, 59 mutants). This follow-up tracks widening the scope back to the full project and fixing the remaining performance issue (coverage capture failure).

## Component Affected

- **File(s)**: `.github/stryker-config.json`, `.github/scripts/run-stryker.cs`
- **Environment**: GitHub Actions `ubuntu-latest`, Stryker 4.13.0

## Current Behavior

- `mutate` scope is limited to 3 files (smoke test). Full project has ~6,181 mutants.
- `coverage-analysis: "off"` forces AllTests mode — every mutant runs all 23,300 tests
- With concurrency 2 and AllTests mode, 59 mutants took 3h 32m. Full scope would need ~350+ hours.
- `break` threshold at 60% means the workflow will fail even with the smoke test (current score: 5.08%)

## Expected Behavior

- Full `**/*.cs` mutate scope with standard exclusions (Log.cs, Constants, etc.)
- Coverage-based testing (`perTest`) working — each mutant only runs its covering tests
- Concurrency at 4+ for reasonable completion time
- Break threshold tuned to realistic target or removed for initial runs

## Impact

- **Developer Experience**: Without full scope, mutation testing only covers 3 files
- **CI/CD Time**: AllTests mode is ~50x slower than perTest mode
- **Reliability**: Break threshold causes false-red on realistic initial scores

## Proposed Solution

### Phase 1: Remove break threshold (quick win)
- [ ] Set `break: 0` in stryker-config.json so the workflow stays green regardless of score
- [ ] Score is still reported in the summary and README badge

### Phase 2: Diagnose coverage capture failure
- [ ] Run Stryker with `--diag` flag to get trace-level coverage capture logs
- [ ] Check if xUnit v3 + Stryker 4.13 has known coverage capture issues (stryker-mutator/stryker-net#3094)
- [ ] Try upgrading to Stryker 4.14.1 (available, shown in logs)
- [ ] Try `coverage-analysis: "perTestInIsolation"` as alternative

### Phase 3: Widen scope incrementally
- [ ] Once perTest works: restore `mutate` to `**/*.cs` with exclusions
- [ ] Increase concurrency from 2 to 4
- [ ] Monitor first full run for timing and memory usage
- [ ] Adjust concurrency based on results

### Phase 4: Tune thresholds
- [ ] After first full-scope run completes, set `break` to observed score minus margin
- [ ] Gradually raise `break` as test quality improves

## Related Issues

- #957 — Parent issue (now closed, all fundamental blockers resolved)
- #73 — [BUG] Fix flaky tests (may help with coverage capture)
- #871 — EPIC v0.13.4 — Critical Bugs & Quality Debt

title: [DEBT] Migrate test projects to Encina.Testing.* wrappers and update outdated NuGet packages
body:
## Type

- [x] Refactoring needed
- [x] Code quality (warnings, analyzers)
- [ ] Failing tests
- [ ] Missing tests
- [ ] Performance optimization
- [ ] Documentation gap
- [ ] Incorrect implementation

## Description

Two related maintenance concerns are being silently reported but not acted on:

1. **Test dependency drift** — the CI workflow `github-actions[bot]` runs a test dependency audit on every push and has been reporting the same findings across multiple PRs (`#1016`, and prior). 5 test projects still reference raw libraries (`FluentAssertions`, `Bogus`, `FsCheck`, `WireMock.Net`, `PactNet`, `Respawn`) despite the existence of standardised wrappers under `src/Encina.Testing.*` (`Shouldly`, `Bogus`, `FsCheck`, `WireMock`, `Pact`, `Respawn`). This is a regression: issue #495 ("Migrate all tests from FluentAssertions to Shouldly") was closed on 2025-12-31 but the `.csproj` files still reference the raw packages.

2. **NuGet package drift** — `dotnet list package --outdated` reports hundreds of outdated packages across the solution, including major-version bumps that may break things (e.g. `Microsoft.Data.SqlClient 6 → 7`, `WireMock.Net 1.25 → 2.2`, `YamlDotNet 16 → 17`).

Tracking both under a single `[DEBT]` so the sub-scopes can be scheduled and executed independently.

## Location

### Scope 1 — Test dependency migration

| Project | Raw packages still referenced | Target wrapper |
|---------|-------------------------------|----------------|
| `tests/Encina.UnitTests/Encina.UnitTests.csproj` | `FluentAssertions`, `FsCheck`, `FsCheck.Xunit.v3`, `Bogus`, `WireMock.Net`, `PactNet` | `Encina.Testing.Shouldly`, `Encina.Testing.FsCheck`, `Encina.Testing.Bogus`, `Encina.Testing.WireMock`, `Encina.Testing.Pact` |
| `tests/Encina.IntegrationTests/Encina.IntegrationTests.csproj` | `FluentAssertions`, `Bogus`, `WireMock.Net`, `PactNet`, `Respawn` | `Encina.Testing.Shouldly`, `Encina.Testing.Bogus`, `Encina.Testing.WireMock`, `Encina.Testing.Pact`, `Encina.Testing.Respawn` |

| `tests/Encina.TestInfrastructure/Encina.TestInfrastructure.csproj` | `Bogus`, `FsCheck` | `Encina.Testing.Bogus`, `Encina.Testing.FsCheck` |

### Scope 2 — NuGet package updates

- **Central config**: `Directory.Packages.props`
- **Affected projects**: every project in the solution (audit reports updates across ~40+ projects).

Highlights (non-exhaustive — see full list in `dotnet list package --outdated`):

**Major-version bumps (likely breaking — evaluate first):**

## Current Behavior

- Every PR triggers the same `Test Dependency Audit` comment from `github-actions[bot]` listing 6 projects needing migration and flagging `Encina.Testing.Shouldly` as a missing package — with no action taken on any PR.
- `Directory.Packages.props` pins versions behind several minor/patch updates and three major-version upgrades.
- Tests still assert with `FluentAssertions` APIs instead of `Shouldly`, contrary to the team standard and closed issue #495.

## Expected Behavior

- **Scope 1**: all 6 test projects reference only `Encina.Testing.*` wrappers; audit reports 0 projects needing migration.
- **Scope 2**: `Directory.Packages.props` tracks latest stable versions; major bumps validated (changelogs read, tests green, benchmarks unaffected). A sustainable cadence is established (e.g. Dependabot/Renovate) so drift does not re-accumulate.

## Root Cause

- #495 declared the FluentAssertions → Shouldly migration complete but never updated the `.csproj` files, only migrated existing assertions.
- `Encina.Testing.Shouldly` was created by #429 but is not referenced by any test project.
- No automated update cadence for NuGet packages (Dependabot / Renovate not configured for the dependency graph). Drift accumulates silently between release preparation windows.

## Proposed Fix

### Scope 1 — Test dependency migration (blocks CI audit noise)

1. Add `Encina.Testing.Shouldly`, `Encina.Testing.Bogus`, `Encina.Testing.FsCheck`, `Encina.Testing.WireMock`, `Encina.Testing.Pact`, `Encina.Testing.Respawn` `ProjectReference`s to the 6 test projects.
2. Remove the corresponding raw `PackageReference`s (`FluentAssertions`, `Bogus`, `FsCheck`, `FsCheck.Xunit.v3`, `WireMock.Net`, `PactNet`, `Respawn`) from each `.csproj`.
3. Adjust any `using` statements and assertion calls that relied on raw APIs not exposed by wrappers (most of the surface is already compatible).
4. Remove the raw packages from `Directory.Packages.props` if no consumer remains.
5. Re-run `dotnet test --configuration Release` across the full matrix; verify audit workflow reports 0 projects needing migration.

### Scope 2 — NuGet updates

1. Start with low-risk minor/patch bumps (EF Core, Testcontainers, analyzers, OTel, SDK). One PR per semantic group to keep reviews tractable.
2. Evaluate major bumps separately, each in its own PR with a written impact assessment:
   - `Microsoft.Data.SqlClient 7.0` — check breaking changes doc, run integration tests against SQL Server.
   - `WireMock.Net 2.2` — API reshape; may require wrapper update in `Encina.Testing.WireMock`.
   - `YamlDotNet 17` — review ecosystem uses.
3. After completing the sweep, configure Dependabot (grouped) or Renovate to keep the solution current.

## Priority

- [ ] **High** — Blocks functionality or causes failures in production
- [x] **Medium** — Should be fixed before 1.0 release (quality hygiene; SqlClient 7.0 has security fixes)
- [ ] **Low** — Nice to have, can be deferred

## Effort Estimate

- [ ] Small (< 1 hour)
- [ ] Medium (1-4 hours)
- [x] Large (> 4 hours) — scope 1: ~3 h; scope 2: ~6–10 h spread across PRs (major bumps each need their own validation)

## Related Issues

- Parent EPIC: #871 ([EPIC] v0.13.4 — Critical Bugs & Quality Debt)
- Historical context: #495 ([DEBT] Migrate all tests from FluentAssertions to Shouldly) — closed but incomplete at the project-reference level
- Historical context: #429 ([FEATURE] Encina.Testing.Shouldly — Open-Source Assertion Extensions) — wrapper created but unused
- Related CI signal: the `Test Dependency Audit` job in `.github/workflows/*` runs on every push; its output is what first surfaced this debt

## Suggested ordering within EPIC #871

Scope 1 (test migration) first — it is isolated, mechanical, silences a noisy CI check, and has no runtime impact. Scope 2 (NuGet) second — major bumps require their own PRs and validation; splits naturally into follow-ups if it grows.

title: [INFRA] Pass per-folder test-case-filter to Stryker to bypass xUnit v3 perTest bug
body:
## Category

- [x] CI/CD Workflow (GitHub Actions)
- [x] Test Infrastructure (fixtures, runners, parallelization)

## Description

The Mutation Tests workflow currently runs each mutant against the full ~23,000-test suite because Stryker.NET cannot use `perTest` coverage analysis with xUnit v3 (upstream bug tracked in #1026). This makes kill results semi-stochastic and adding targeted tests yields no measurable improvement — see the empirical evidence in the closing comment of #962.

We can bypass the upstream bug by supplying Stryker with a **manual test-to-source mapping** based on Encina's namespace conventions. Test projects mirror source structure: `src/Encina/Sharding/Migrations/Strategies/*.cs` is tested exclusively by `tests/Encina.UnitTests/Core/Sharding/Migrations/Strategies/*Tests.cs`. So when Stryker is asked to mutate a given folder, we can narrow the `test-case-filter` to only the tests whose namespace mirrors that folder. Each mutant then runs the ~20-50 relevant tests instead of 23,000.

## Component Affected

- **File(s)**:
  - `.github/workflows/mutation-tests.yml` — the `Select mutation scope` step needs to also emit a `TEST_FILTER` output
  - `.github/scripts/run-stryker.cs` — forward the `--test-case-filter` argument when provided
- **Environment**: GitHub Actions `ubuntu-latest`, Stryker.NET 4.14.0, xUnit v3

## Current Behavior

- `custom_scope` input (added in #962) narrows the `--mutate` glob to one folder
- `test-case-filter` in `stryker-config.json` is fixed to the three declared test projects' namespaces (`FullyQualifiedName~Encina.UnitTests|...~Encina.PropertyTests|...~Encina.ContractTests`) — every run ignores that folder's actual scope
- With `coverage-analysis: "off"`, Stryker runs every test against every mutant, which both slows the run (~3 min/mutant × ~60 mutants ≈ 3 h) and makes kills non-deterministic
- Run [24584286635](https://github.com/dlrivada/Encina/actions/runs/24584286635): 1 killed / 58 survived despite 26 mutation-targeted tests being in place

## Expected Behavior

- The `Select mutation scope` step also emits a `TEST_FILTER` output derived from the mutation scope:
  - `**/Sharding/Migrations/Strategies/*.cs` → `FullyQualifiedName~Sharding.Migrations.Strategies`
  - `**/Pipeline/Behaviors/*.cs` → `FullyQualifiedName~Pipeline.Behaviors`
  - ... and so on for each of the 17 rotation entries
- The `Run mutation tests` step passes `--test-case-filter "$TEST_FILTER"` to Stryker, overriding the config value
- Each mutant runs only tests from the matching namespace → ~20-50 per mutant instead of 23,000
- Per-mutant time drops from ~3 min to ~5-10 s
- A folder run completes in ~5-10 min instead of ~3 h
- Kills become deterministic because only tests that actually touch the mutated code path execute

## Impact

- **Developer Experience**: contributors adding mutation-targeted tests see immediate kill-count improvements
- **CI/CD Time**: per-folder run drops from ~3 h to ~5-10 min — ~20× reduction in runner time
- **Reliability**: kill count becomes a stable signal of test quality (no more "3 → 1" regressions from upstream version changes)
- **Unlocks #1027** (matrix-parallel full-project coverage)

## Proposed Solution

### Phase 1: Folder-to-filter map in the workflow

- [ ] Extend the `FOLDERS` array in `.github/workflows/mutation-tests.yml` into a parallel structure that pairs each scope glob with its test filter. Options: two arrays (`FOLDERS` + `FILTERS`) indexed together, or a single associative array.
- [ ] Derive the filter from the scope glob automatically where possible — `**/Sharding/Migrations/Strategies/*.cs` ↔ `Sharding.Migrations.Strategies` is a clean mapping. Edge cases (`**/Core/*.cs` is ambiguous) can be hand-mapped.
- [ ] Emit the filter as a step output alongside the scope.

### Phase 2: Forward filter to Stryker

- [ ] Modify the `Run mutation tests` step to pass `--test-case-filter "$FILTER"` to `run-stryker.cs` when the filter is non-empty.
- [ ] `run-stryker.cs` already forwards unknown args to Stryker; verify no change needed there.

### Phase 3: Validate against the Strategies folder

- [ ] Trigger the workflow with `custom_scope='**/Sharding/Migrations/Strategies/*.cs'`. Expected: kill count jumps from 1 → somewhere in the 20-40 range (of 59 mutants), matching what the 26 targeted tests were designed to catch. Run should complete in ~5-10 min instead of ~3 h.

### Phase 4: Document

- [ ] Update `docs/testing/mutation-measurement-methodology.md`: new section "Per-folder test filter" explaining the manual mapping and its relationship to the upstream perTest bug.
- [ ] Update `CLAUDE.md` "Mutation Testing System" section.

## Risks

- **False negatives**: a contract test in a different namespace that would legitimately kill a mutant in the target folder won't run. For the current 17 rotation folders, source-to-test mapping is tight (dedicated `*Tests.cs` per source file), so the risk is small. If encountered, the fix is to broaden the filter for that specific folder.
- **Namespace drift**: if test namespaces get renamed without updating the mapping, kills silently disappear. Mitigation: the methodology doc documents the mapping convention; reviewers should catch mismatches.

## Related Issues

- #957 — Mutation workflow stabilization (closed)
- #962 — Scope widening + cited-by (closed)
- #1026 — Blocked-upstream: Stryker.NET xUnit v3 perTest bug (this issue is the workaround)
- Unlocks #1027 — Matrix-parallel full-project mutation coverage

## Repro (baseline, before fix)

```bash
gh workflow run "Mutation Tests" --ref main \
  -f custom_scope='**/Sharding/Migrations/Strategies/*.cs'
# Wait ~3h. Observe: 1 killed / 58 survived.
```

title: [INFRA] Dependabot nuget job hits 1h timeout, blocking automated security updates
body:
## Category

- [x] CI/CD Workflow (GitHub Actions)
- [x] Repository Configuration (branch rules, templates)

## Description

The scheduled Dependabot **nuget** updater hits the 1-hour GitHub job timeout before producing PRs. Without successful runs, security advisories against existing dependencies don't reach `main` automatically — they have to be patched by hand whenever a new GHSA lands.

This was discovered while investigating the workflow failures of 2026-04-24 to 2026-04-27 (CI Full, CodeQL, Benchmarks, Load Tests, Mutation Tests). All 5 failed because three packages with new GHSA advisories tripped `NU1902`/`NU1904` and `TreatWarningsAsErrors` escalates them to errors. Dependabot should have raised the bump PR before the audit fired in CI; instead the most recent nuget run was cancelled at the 1h mark (see Current Behavior).

## Component Affected

- **File(s)**: [`.github/dependabot.yml`](.github/dependabot.yml), [`Directory.Packages.props`](Directory.Packages.props)
- **Environment**: GitHub Actions (Dependabot-managed runner)

## Current Behavior

The most recent scheduled `nuget` run started at `2026-04-27T13:46:25Z`, ran for ~55 minutes inside the `Run Dependabot` step, and was cancelled at `2026-04-27T14:41:39Z` — before producing any PR.

Run: [24998763697](https://github.com/dlrivada/Encina/actions/runs/24998763697).

Likely cause: the repository has ~150+ `.csproj` files across `src/`, `tests/`, `tools/`, and Dependabot must enumerate the dependency graph for each one. With Central Package Management adding cross-project resolution, the analysis exceeds the 1-hour wall clock.

Knock-on effects observed:
- The 3 GHSA advisories patched in #1041 (DataProtection critical, OpenTelemetry moderate ×2) had to be bumped manually.
- Any future advisories landing in dependencies sit unpatched until somebody runs into a red CI.
- The companion `dotnet test` audit only catches them after they break workflows.

## Expected Behavior

Dependabot completes within the timeout and opens PRs automatically when:
1. A package gets a new GHSA advisory, or
2. A grouped update is due per cooldown.

PRs should ship within 24h of an advisory becoming public, not hand-rolled by whoever notices the red CI.

## Impact

- **Developer Experience**: Manual bumps for security advisories instead of reviewing auto-PRs. ~30-60 min per incident, plus the time to debug the failing CI in the first place.
- **CI/CD Time**: N/A — the nuget Dependabot job itself is what's breaking. Other workflows are unaffected directly, but they break later when audit warnings escalate.
- **Reliability**: **Security posture is compromised** — automated security updates are the canonical mitigation path, and that path is currently broken. Critical CVEs (e.g. CVE-2026-40372 in DataProtection) sat unpatched until the regular CI run revealed them.

## Proposed Solution

Investigate and apply one or more of the following, in order of preference:

1. **Group updates aggressively** in [`.github/dependabot.yml`](.github/dependabot.yml) — many updates analyzed together is faster than individual ones. Suggested groups: `microsoft-extensions` (all `Microsoft.Extensions.*`), `efcore` (all `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.*`), `aspnetcore` (all `Microsoft.AspNetCore.*`), `opentelemetry` (`OpenTelemetry.*`), `aws-sdk` (`AWSSDK.*`), `azure-sdk` (`Azure.*`), `testcontainers` (`Testcontainers.*`), `xunit` (`xunit.*`).
2. **Split by directory or ecosystem** — define multiple `package-ecosystem: \"nuget\"` entries scoped to `src/`, `tests/`, `tools/` separately so each runs within budget.
3. **Use cooldown** to reduce churn (`open-pull-requests-limit`, `cooldown.default-days`) and let updates batch up across runs.
4. **Disable transitive analysis** if Dependabot supports a flag — verify against current Dependabot config schema.
5. **Switch to Renovate** if the above fail to bring runs under 60 min — it has more granular timeouts and richer batching, but the migration is non-trivial.

The goal is a **green nuget Dependabot run completing in <60 min**, producing grouped PRs with sensible cadence.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Scheduled `nuget` Dependabot run completes within the GitHub timeout
- [ ] At least one auto-generated update PR lands successfully on `main`
- [ ] No regression in update coverage (still picks up all 200+ central packages)
- [ ] Dependabot dashboard / job logs free of timeouts for at least 2 consecutive scheduled runs

## Related Issues / PRs

- #1041 — Manual security bump that motivated this issue (DataProtection 10.0.7, OpenTelemetry 1.15.3). What Dependabot would have raised automatically had it run successfully.
- #1026 — Sibling INFRA issue under v0.13.4 (mutation testing AllTests workaround); shares the "operational quality debt blocking automation" theme.

title: [DEBT] Register Encina.OpenTelemetry EventId range 7000-7099 in EventIdRanges.cs
body:
## Type

- [x] Code quality (warnings, analyzers)
- [x] Incorrect implementation (violates [ADR-021](docs/architecture/adr/021-eventid-uniqueness-enforcement.md))

## Description

`Encina.OpenTelemetry/Resharding/ReshardingLogMessages.cs` uses `EventId` values **7000–7009** (10 events: `ReshardingStarted`, `ReshardingPhaseStarted`, `ReshardingPhaseCompleted`, `ReshardingCopyProgress`, `ReshardingCdcLagUpdate`, `ReshardingVerificationResult`, `ReshardingCutoverStarted`, `ReshardingCutoverCompleted`, `ReshardingFailed`, `ReshardingRolledBack`), but **no corresponding range is registered** in `src/Encina/Diagnostics/EventIdRanges.cs`.

This violates [ADR-021 — EventId Uniqueness Enforcement Rule](docs/architecture/adr/021-eventid-uniqueness-enforcement.md) which mandates that every `[LoggerMessage]` EventId range be registered in the central registry before use, validated at test time by `EventIdUniquenessRule` in `Encina.Testing.Architecture`.

It's currently a silent gap — there's no test failure because the architecture test only verifies `EventIdsWithinRegisteredRanges` for ranges that are *registered*. Unregistered EventIds slip through. The right fix is to register the range so the architecture test catches future drift.

## Location

- **File(s)**:
  - `src/Encina.OpenTelemetry/Resharding/ReshardingLogMessages.cs` (uses 7000-7009)
  - `src/Encina/Diagnostics/EventIdRanges.cs` (missing the registration)
- **Package(s)**: `Encina.OpenTelemetry`, `Encina` (for the registry)

## Current Behavior

`ReshardingLogMessages` emits structured logs with EventId values 7000-7009, but those values are not declared in `EventIdRanges.cs`. The architecture tests in `Encina.Testing.Architecture` (`AssertEventIdsAreGloballyUnique`, `AssertEventIdsWithinRegisteredRanges`, `AssertNoRangeOverlaps`) cannot enforce uniqueness or correctness against this range — it's effectively invisible to the registry-based enforcement.

## Expected Behavior

`EventIdRanges.cs` declares a range for `Encina.OpenTelemetry`'s resharding log messages, e.g.:

```csharp
// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
// Observability (7000-7099)
// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

/// <summary>Encina.OpenTelemetry — resharding orchestration log messages.</summary>
public static readonly (int Min, int Max) OpenTelemetryResharding = (7000, 7099);
```

After registration, `EventIdUniquenessRule.AssertEventIdsWithinRegisteredRanges()` validates that all 10 emitted EventIds fall within `[7000, 7099]`, and any future addition of a `[LoggerMessage]` outside that range — or with a colliding ID — fails the architecture test suite.

The 7000-7099 block is reserved for `Encina.OpenTelemetry` more broadly (single 100-slot range covers resharding today and leaves room for future log sources in the package). Future Encina.OpenTelemetry features (e.g., OTLP wiring telemetry from #1043 if structured logging is added there, the OTLP health check from #1049) can carve sub-ranges within 7000-7099 if needed.

## Root Cause

`Encina.OpenTelemetry`'s resharding logging predated ADR-021 (the EventId Uniqueness Enforcement decision). When the rule was introduced and the central registry was populated for compliance/security/messaging packages, the OpenTelemetry resharding range wasn't migrated. The architecture test only catches collisions and out-of-range usage *for registered ranges* — silent unregistered usage slipped through.

## Proposed Fix

1. Add a `OpenTelemetryResharding = (7000, 7099)` entry to `EventIdRanges.cs`, in a new "Observability" section between Domain Events / Event Sourcing (2500-2699) and the Security/Compliance bands (8000+).
2. Update the XML doc comment on `ReshardingLogMessages` to reference the registered range.
3. Verify `EventIdUniquenessRule.AssertEventIdsWithinRegisteredRanges()` passes for the new entry.
4. Update the "Current Range Map (Quick Reference)" table in CLAUDE.md to include the new entry.

## Priority

- [x] **Low** — Nice to have, can be deferred. Doesn't block functionality but is a known gap that should be fixed before 1.0 to keep the registry comprehensive.

## Effort Estimate

- [x] Small (< 1 hour)

## Related Issues

- #1043 — Wire OTLP exporter (mentions this gap as out-of-scope)
- #1049 — OTLP collector reachability health check (will need its own EventId allocation; once this issue lands, that allocation has a documented home)
- ADR-021 — EventId Uniqueness Enforcement Rule

title: [DEBT] HMACValidationPipelineBehavior fails open without HttpContext; make skipping validation an explicit opt-out
body:
## Type

- [x] Incorrect implementation

## Description

`HMACValidationPipelineBehavior` skips signature validation for a `[RequireSignature]` request when there is no `HttpContext` (`src/Encina.Security.AntiTampering/Pipeline/HMACValidationPipelineBehavior.cs:127-130`). The type's XML remarks (lines 32-36) describe this as intended, so that the same request types can run in background jobs and tests, and `HMACValidationPipelineBehaviorTests.Handle_NoHttpContext_PassesThrough` asserts it.

It is still a fail-open default for a security control that the request type opted into. Any non-HTTP entry point bypasses it silently: a Blazor Server circuit (#1148), a message consumer, a scheduled job, or a gRPC or SignalR path without an `HttpContext`.

## Location

- **File(s)**:
  - `src/Encina.Security.AntiTampering/Pipeline/HMACValidationPipelineBehavior.cs:32-36`
  - `src/Encina.Security.AntiTampering/Pipeline/HMACValidationPipelineBehavior.cs:127-130`
- **Package(s)**: Encina.Security.AntiTampering

## Current Behavior

With no `HttpContext`, the request is passed through without validation.

## Expected Behavior

The default fails closed. Skipping validation outside HTTP is an explicit, per-request or per-option decision, for example `[RequireSignature(SkipWhenNoHttpContext = true)]` or `AntiTamperingOptions.SkipWhenNoHttpContext`, and it is logged when used.

## Root Cause

A convenience for background jobs and tests became the global default.

## Proposed Fix

- Fail closed by default.
- Add the explicit opt-out.
- Update the existing test and the XML remarks.

Reproduction on branch `spike/verify-request-context` (commit `30b8a218`): `Handle_RequireSignatureAttribute_NoHttpContext_ShouldRejectInsteadOfPassingThrough` in `tests/Encina.UnitTests/Security/AntiTampering/HMACValidationPipelineBehaviorNoHttpContextSpikeTests.cs`.

## Priority

- [x] **Medium** - Should be fixed before 1.0 release

## Effort Estimate

- [x] Small (< 1 hour)

## Related Issues

- #1148
- #1147
- SPEC-002 (in preparation)

title: [BUG] Retention enforcement erases every data category of an entity, not only the expired one
body:
## Description

When a retention record expires, the enforcement cycle erases **all** personal data of the entity, not only the data category whose retention period expired.

`RetentionEnforcementService` builds an `ErasureScope` that sets only `Reason`. `DefaultDataErasureExecutor.ApplyScope` (`src/Encina.Compliance.DataSubjectRights/Erasure/DefaultDataErasureExecutor.cs:188-198`) keeps every location when `Categories` is null. The cycle also passes the retention record's `EntityId` as the executor's `subjectId`, but the executor treats it as a data-subject id, which is a different thing.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Track the same entity under two retention records:
   - `contact`, with a retention of 1 year;
   - `clinical`, with a retention of 5 years.
2. Let the `contact` record expire and run an enforcement cycle.
3. Every personal-data location of the entity is erased, including the clinical data, 4 years early.

## Expected Behavior

- The erasure scope carries the expired record's `DataCategory`.
- The executor erases only locations of that category, for the correct subject/entity mapping.
- Data of other categories, still within their retention period, is untouched.

## Actual Behavior

The whole entity is erased.

## Environment

- **Encina Version**: main (pre-1.0); found in the adversarial review of #1157
- **.NET Version**: .NET 10.0
- **OS**: any
- **Package(s) Affected**: Encina.Compliance.Retention, Encina.Compliance.DataSubjectRights

## Code Sample

```csharp
var erasureScope = new ErasureScope { Reason = ErasureReason.NoLongerNecessary }; // no Categories
await erasureExecutor.EraseAsync(record.EntityId, erasureScope, cancellationToken);
```

## Stack Trace

```text
Not applicable.
```

## Additional Context

- **Why it matters:** this breaks the reference use case of SPEC-002 (#1156), where a clinical record must be kept at least 5 years (Ley 41/2002, art. 17) while other data expires sooner.
- **Related:** #1144 (crypto-shredding erases every key of a subject), which has the same root problem: erasure is not scoped by category.
- **Also to fix:** the `EntityId` vs `subjectId` mismatch.

title: [BUG] About 28 call sites resolve an unregistered IRequestContext from DI and always get null
body:
## Description

About 28 call sites resolve `IRequestContext` straight from the service provider with `sp.GetService<IRequestContext>()`. Nothing registers `IRequestContext` in DI, so every one of those calls returns `null`. Some call sites also capture the value when the service is constructed, and some of those services may be singletons. Features that depend on the caller's identity or tenant therefore run with no identity at all: repository and sharding tenant filters, ABAC policy administration and secret-access auditing.

Since #1147 (PR #1162), the context flows through the core `IRequestContextAccessor` (AsyncLocal, ambient per dispatch). The correct pattern is to inject `IRequestContextAccessor` and read `RequestContext` at the moment the context is needed.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Register a repository through `Encina.ADO.*`, `Encina.Dapper.*` or `Encina.MongoDB` with tenancy enabled, or register `Encina.Security.ABAC` with `PersistentPolicyAdministrationPoint`, `Encina.Security.Secrets` with auditing, or `Encina.Compliance.NIS2`.
2. Call it from inside a request that has a user and a tenant.
3. The component sees a `null` context. For example, `DefaultNIS2ComplianceValidator.cs:73` reads it as absent.

## Expected Behavior

Each component reads the current context from `IRequestContextAccessor` when it needs it. It gets the ambient context or the one passed explicitly to `Send`, and never a snapshot taken when it was constructed.

## Actual Behavior

`GetService<IRequestContext>()` returns `null`, so identity-dependent logic takes its no-context branch.

## Environment

- **Encina Version**: main (pre-1.0), found during the adversarial review of #1162
- **.NET Version**: .NET 10.0
- **OS**: any
- **Package(s) Affected**: Encina.ADO.*, Encina.Dapper.*, Encina.MongoDB (repository and sharding registrations), Encina.Security.ABAC (`PersistentPolicyAdministrationPoint`), Encina.Security.Secrets (`AuditedSecretReaderDecorator`), Encina.Compliance.NIS2 (`DefaultNIS2ComplianceValidator`)

## Code Sample

```csharp
var context = sp.GetService<IRequestContext>(); // always null: IRequestContext is never registered
```

## Stack Trace

```text
Not applicable.
```

## Additional Context

- **How to find every call site:** run `Select-String -Pattern 'GetService<IRequestContext>'` across `src/`.
- **Fix:** inject `IRequestContextAccessor` and read it at use time. Do not register `IRequestContext` as a transient, because that hands out a stale snapshot.
- **Related:** #1147 and PR #1162.

title: [INFRA] Agent system review: model choice, pre-PR self-review, main-checkout guard, edit safety, turn limits, issue drafting, brief skill, command hook, proportional delegation
body:
## Category

- [x] Developer Tooling (CLI, scripts, dev containers)
- [x] Other: Claude Code agents, hooks and skills (`.claude/`)

## Description

This issue reviews how the orchestrator/worker model behaved over the 2026-09-22/24 sessions (about 20 PRs and 40 issues) and lists nine improvements. The maintainer approved all nine on 2026-09-24, to be applied in this order:

1. **Model choice.** Default workers to Sonnet. Use Opus only when the brief justifies it: an unknown root cause, or a design-heavy task.
2. **Self-review before hand-off.** Workers may spawn `adversarial-reviewer` on their own diff before reporting, so findings are fixed before the PR opens. Today every PR goes through a review → fix → re-push → CI loop.
3. **Main-checkout guard.** Workers wrote into the main checkout three times (relative paths through `[IO.File]`). A hook detects such writes and blocks or warns at once.
4. **Edit tool only for source files.** Workers edit `.cs` and other source files only with the Edit/Write tools, never with PowerShell `-replace` or `[IO.File]` writes. A PowerShell replace corrupted six files in #1159.
5. **Turn limits.** Raise `mechanical-fixer` from 30 to 50 turns and `issue-worker` from 80 to 120. Both limits were hit this session, and each resume re-reads context.
6. **Issue bodies from workers.** Workers write follow-up issue bodies in the exact template format to files and list their paths. The orchestrator then only runs `gh issue create`. The local model can draft bodies with the `local-ai-task` skill. The goal is to keep large issue texts out of the orchestrator's context.
7. **`worker-brief` skill.** A skill that holds the fixed part of every brief: worktree and absolute paths, no push, changelog fragments, verification, delegation, report format. The orchestrator then writes only the task-specific part.
8. **Prohibited commands.** Extend the worker hooks to reject the commands that CLAUDE.md prohibits (`curl`, `grep`, `sed`, `awk`, `head`, `tail`, `python`, and others). Workers used some of them unnoticed.
9. **Proportional delegation.** Change the rule from mandatory to proportional. Nested delegation is required when it pays off: replication across providers, many files, root-causing CI. Inline edits are fine for a few lines. Workers mostly did small edits inline anyway, and a `mechanical-fixer` start costs about 90–110k tokens.

## Component Affected

- `.claude/agents/*.md`
- `.claude/hooks/*.ps1` and `.claude/hooks/tests/Test-Hooks.ps1`
- `.claude/skills/`
- `.claude/agents/README.md`
- `docs/engineering/AI-DEVELOPMENT-MODEL.md`
- the orchestrator memory

## Current Behavior

- Most workers run on Opus.
- Reviews happen only after the PR is open.
- There is no guard against writes to the main checkout.
- Text replacement in PowerShell is allowed on source files.
- Workers hit their turn limits.
- The orchestrator writes every issue body.
- Briefs repeat the same boilerplate.
- Prohibited Unix commands pass unnoticed.
- The delegation rule is absolute and mostly ignored.

## Expected Behavior

The behaviour described in items 1–9 above, enforced mechanically where possible (hooks with regression tests) and documented in the agent definitions and `AI-DEVELOPMENT-MODEL.md`.

## Impact

- **Tokens:** fewer tokens used, through model choice and less orchestrator context.
- **CI:** fewer CI runs, because review happens before the PR.
- **Safety:** no stray writes and no corrupted files.
- **Fewer resumes:** no stops at the turn limit.

## Proposed Solution

One tooling PR that implements items 1–9 with hook regression tests. It is based on #1178 (git clone allowed) and #1179 (docs agents), and gets rebased after they merge.

## Related Issues

- #1131, #1139 (issue-worker and hooks)
- #1178, #1179

title: [DEBT] BulkOperationsEF still dispatches to Oracle and SQLite implementations removed from scope
body:
## Type
- [ ] Failing tests
- [ ] Missing tests
- [ ] Performance optimization
- [ ] Refactoring needed
- [ ] Documentation gap
- [ ] Incorrect implementation
- [x] Code quality (warnings, analyzers)
- [ ] Other

## Description
`Encina.EntityFrameworkCore.BulkOperations.BulkOperationsEF` dispatches to `BulkOperationsEFOracle` and `BulkOperationsEFSqlite`, and its `CreateProviderImplementation` switch references `OracleConnection` and `SqliteConnection`. Oracle was removed pre-1.0 (ADR-009) and SQLite too (ADR-024). This is dead code that keeps references to providers outside the supported matrix.

## Location
`src/Encina.EntityFrameworkCore/BulkOperations/`

## Current Behavior
The `BulkOperationsEF` class includes logic to detect and dispatch to Oracle and SQLite providers, even though these providers are no longer part of the supported matrix. The `CreateProviderImplementation` method contains switch cases for `OracleConnection` and `SqliteConnection`.

## Expected Behavior
The `BulkOperationsEF` class should only dispatch to supported providers: SQL Server, PostgreSQL, and MySQL. References to Oracle and SQLite should be removed to align with the current provider support matrix.

## Root Cause
The removal of Oracle (ADR-009) and SQLite (ADR-024) providers did not include a complete cleanup of the bulk operations dispatch logic and related implementation classes.

## Proposed Fix
Remove the Oracle and SQLite branches from the `CreateProviderImplementation` switch statement and delete the corresponding implementation classes (`BulkOperationsEFOracle` and `BulkOperationsEFSqlite`) if still present. Retain only the logic for SQL Server, PostgreSQL, and MySQL.

## Priority
- [ ] **High** - Must be fixed before release
- [ ] **Medium** - Should be fixed in the current release
- [x] **Low** - Nice to have, can be deferred

## Effort Estimate
- [x] Small (< 1 hour)
- [ ] Medium (1-4 hours)
- [ ] Large (> 4 hours)

## Related Issues
- ADR-009
- ADR-024
- #83

title: [BUG] AddEncinaMongoDB registers InboxOrchestrator without InboxOptions
body:
## Description
The `AddEncinaMongoDB` method in the `Encina.MongoDB` package registers `InboxOrchestrator`, which depends on `InboxOptions`, but fails to register `InboxOptions` itself. Consequently, if the inbox is enabled, resolving `InboxOrchestrator` results in a failure. This is inconsistent with other providers, which correctly register the options.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Call `AddEncinaMongoDB` with the inbox feature enabled.
2. Build the service provider with `ValidateOnBuild` enabled.
3. Attempt to resolve `InboxOrchestrator`.

## Expected Behavior
MongoDB should register `InboxOptions` similarly to the other 9 providers. A dependency injection test should be able to resolve `InboxOrchestrator` with the inbox enabled without error.

## Actual Behavior
Resolving `InboxOrchestrator` fails because `InboxOptions` is not registered in the service collection.

## Environment
Encina main (pre-1.0), .NET 10, Encina.MongoDB

## Code Sample
Not applicable.

## Stack Trace
Not captured.

## Additional Context
The PR #1259 DI test registers `InboxOptions` itself, with a comment, to test only the serializer; remove that workaround when this is fixed. Found while fixing the review findings of PR #1259.

## Root Cause
Missing options registration in the MongoDB ServiceCollectionExtensions.
